security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU TCG, write_menvcfg() and write_henvcfg() store the ADUE bit without calling tlb_flush() or tb_flush(). The page table walker (get_physical_address) reads menvcfg/henvcfg only on TLB miss, so TLB hits use cached translations resolved under the old ADUE value. Specifically, a TLB entry filled when ADUE=1 (hardware sets A/D bits during walk) persists after ADUE→0 (Svade: fault on unset A/D), allowing accesses through stale TLB entries that would fault on real hardware where the new ADUE interpretation applies.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: write_menvcfg\b|\bwrite_henvcfg\b.*\{ — no tlb_flush\(|tb_flush\( when menvcfg_cfg.ADUE or HENVCFG_ADUE bit toggles
security_spec.summary: QEMU TCG write_menvcfg/write_henvcfg do not flush TLBs on ADUE changes, violating spec mandate that ADUE settings are 'permitted to be cached in a TLB' and require software SFENCE.VMA for synchronization — stale TLB entries can bypass A/D page faults that real hardware would raise.
